First steps

Kepler pressed a foot into the red ground. Comet checked the oxygen timer. Neither of them said it, but they were both thinking the same thing: where do we even start?

pages.title: The trip
pages.html:
The trip

About 7 months from Earth. A real trip usually takes 6 to 9. Ships leave only about every 26 months — when Earth and Mars line up. Help will not arrive soon.

This book is Kepler's mission log. Mars days are called sols. One sol lasts about twenty-four hours and forty minutes. Each log entry starts with the Sol number and the time.

pages.title: Sol 1 · Mars day 1 · 06:14
pages.html:
Sol 1 · Mars day 1 · 06:14

We landed on Mars. The landing pod is bent, but it still holds air well enough to climb out. We leave the ship to explore an empty planet. The air outside is too thin to breathe. Inside, we have about six hours of oxygen left.

pages.title: Sol 1 · 06:31

Sol 1 · 06:31

Comet nearly opened a helmet to go outside. Outside, the air pressure is less than 1% of Earth’s — almost nothing. One breath out there would end the mission. Kepler sealed the latch. Going outside was canceled.

pages.title: Field note · Thin air
pages.html:
Field note · Thin air

Earth's air is thick and full of the oxygen we need. Mars air is almost all carbon dioxide — the gas we breathe out — and less than 1% as thick.

pages.title: Sol 1 · 07:02
pages.html:
Sol 1 · 07:02

We scratched a list in the dust of what we have and what we need. We need oxygen. We have ice, sunlight, and scrap metal. There is no ready oxygen tank on board. We could split water into oxygen if we find ice.

pages.title: Field note · Ice under dust
pages.html:
Field note · Ice under dust

Water ice often hides under the red dust on Mars. Dig a little, melt it, and a colony has water to drink, grow plants, and make oxygen.

pages.title: Field note · Splitting water
pages.html:
Field note · Splitting water

Electrolysis means using electricity to split water. You get 2 parts hydrogen gas and 1 part oxygen — and that oxygen is what we breathe.

A habitat only works if the air stays sealed inside. Tap the shell: a clear ring means it is sealed; a dull sound means there is a crack to find and fix.

Sol 2 · 05:03

The pressurized bubble — our sealed room with thicker air — is stable. Helmets came off indoors. A sprout stands upright in protected soil. Outside is still deadly. First breath of indoor air is logged.
